analysis.title: Broken Object Level Authorization (IDOR) on Shopping Basket
analysis.vulnerability_explanation: The endpoint /rest/basket/{id} returns customer cart details based solely on the URL path ID parameter. Requesting basket ID 1 using User B credentials successfully returned User A's private product inventory without proper ownership verification.
analysis.technical_root_cause: The application fails to verify whether req.user.id matches the owner (basket.UserId) before returning the shopping basket record from the database.
analysis.potential_impact: Unauthorized customer PII disclosure, order history leakage, and horizontal privilege escalation across tenant accounts.

supporting_evidence.description: User B was able to view User A's private shopping basket without authorization.
supporting_evidence.observed_behavior: HTTP 200 OK returned with User A's cart data containing Apple Juice product item.
supporting_evidence.expected_behavior: HTTP 403 Forbidden with Access Denied error.

severity_assessment.potential_impact: Complete unauthorized disclosure of arbitrary user shopping carts and personal item selections.
severity_assessment.severity_rationale: CVSS:3.1 base score 6.5 (High) due to network accessibility, low attack complexity, low privileges required, and significant confidentiality impact.

remediation_recommendation.recommended_fix: Enforce object-level access control verifying session identity matches resource ownership prior to database retrieval.
remediation_recommendation.why_fix_works: Explicitly checks authenticated session identity against resource owner identity at the controller layer before releasing entity data.
remediation_recommendation.retesting_procedure: Authenticate as User B and send HTTP GET /rest/basket/1. Verify status code is 403 Forbidden with an access denied payload.
regression_testing_recommendations: Implement integration tests asserting that non-owner tokens receive 403 for /rest/basket/:id.
Add automated differential role scans to CI pipeline.
